questions.s: An infinite geometric series has common ratio q. Which condition on q is required for the series to have a finite sum?
questions.e: Sₙ = a₁(1 − qⁿ)/(1 − q) tends to a₁/(1 − q) only when qⁿ → 0, i.e. |q| < 1 (and a geometric ratio is never 0). q < 1 allows q = −2, whose terms grow in size, and |q| ≤ 1 allows q = ±1, which do not converge.

questions.s: The three angles of a triangle form an arithmetic sequence, and the smallest angle is 30°. What is the largest angle?
questions.e: If the angles are 60° − d, 60°, 60° + d, their sum is 180°, so the middle angle is 60°. With 60° − d = 30°, d = 30° and the largest angle is 90°. The value 60° is the middle angle.

questions.s: Here lg denotes the logarithm to base 10. What is the value of lg(2/1) + lg(3/2) + lg(4/3) + … + lg(100/99)?
questions.e: lg((k + 1)/k) = lg(k + 1) − lg k, so the sum telescopes to lg 100 − lg 1 = 2. Stopping the telescoping at lg 99 forgets that the last term contributes lg 100.

questions.s: What is the value of 1 × 2 + 2 × 3 + 3 × 4 + … + 10 × 11?
questions.e: k(k + 1) = k² + k, so the sum is (1² + … + 10²) + (1 + … + 10) = 385 + 55 = 440; equivalently n(n + 1)(n + 2)/3 = 10 × 11 × 12/3 = 440. The value 385 is only the sum of the squares, and 572 goes up to 11 × 12.

questions.s: A culture starts with 100 bacteria and the number doubles every hour. How many bacteria are there after 5 hours?
questions.e: The counts 100, 200, 400, … are geometric with ratio 2, so after 5 hours there are 100 × 2⁵ = 3200. The value 1600 is after 4 hours, and 1000 multiplies by 2 × 5 = 10 instead of 2⁵ = 32.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of a sequence {aₙ} is Sₙ = 2ⁿ − 1. What is a₁² + a₂² + … + aₙ²?
questions.e: aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = 2ⁿ⁻¹ (and a₁ = 1 fits), so aₙ² = 4ⁿ⁻¹ is geometric with first term 1 and ratio 4. The sum is (4ⁿ − 1)/(4 − 1) = (4ⁿ − 1)/3. Squaring the sum, (2ⁿ − 1)², is not the sum of the squares.

questions.s: What is the 20th term of the arithmetic sequence 5, 9, 13, 17, …?
questions.e: a₁ = 5 and d = 4, so a₂₀ = 5 + 19 × 4 = 81. Using 20 × 4 gives 85, and 77 is the 19th term.

questions.s: What is the common ratio of the geometric sequence 2, −6, 18, −54, …?
questions.e: q = a₂/a₁ = −6/2 = −3, and each later term is also −3 times the one before. The value −1/3 is a₁/a₂, the ratio taken the wrong way round, and −8 is the difference a₂ − a₁, not a ratio.

questions.s: A sequence has general term aₙ = (2n − 1)/(n + 1). What is a₄?
questions.e: a₄ = (2 × 4 − 1)/(4 + 1) = 7/5. Dividing by n instead of n + 1 gives 7/4, and using 2n + 1 in the numerator gives 9/5.

questions.s: The first 9 terms of an arithmetic sequence have mean 7, and a₁ = 3. What is a₉?
questions.e: For 9 terms the mean equals the middle term, so a₅ = 7; then 4d = 7 − 3 gives d = 1 and a₉ = 3 + 8 = 11. Equivalently (a₁ + a₉)/2 = 7 gives a₉ = 14 − 3 = 11. The value 14 forgets to subtract a₁.

questions.s: What is the sum of the infinite series 1 − 1/3 + 1/9 − 1/27 + …?
questions.e: a₁ = 1 and q = −1/3, so S = 1/(1 − (−1/3)) = 1/(4/3) = 3/4. Ignoring the sign of q gives 1/(2/3) = 3/2.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 2 and a non-zero common difference, and a₁, a₃, a₇ form a geometric sequence. What is the sum of the first 10 terms of the arithmetic sequence?
questions.e: (2 + 2d)² = 2(2 + 6d) gives 4 + 8d + 4d² = 4 + 12d, so 4d² = 4d and d = 1 (d ≠ 0). Then aₙ = n + 1 and S₁₀ = 10(2 + 11)/2 = 65. Forgetting to halve gives 130.

questions.s: A machine worth 80 000 yuan loses 25 % of its value each year. What is it worth after 2 years?
questions.e: Each year the value is multiplied by 0.75, so after 2 years it is 80 000 × 0.75² = 80 000 × 9/16 = 45 000 yuan. Subtracting 20 000 yuan each year (25 % of the original value) gives 40 000 yuan, which treats the loss as linear.

questions.s: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 2 and aₙ₊₁ − aₙ = 3ⁿ for n ≥ 1. What is its general term?
questions.e: Adding the differences, aₙ = 2 + (3 + 3² + … + 3ⁿ⁻¹) = 2 + (3ⁿ − 3)/2 = (3ⁿ + 1)/2 (check: a₂ = 5, a₃ = 14). The formula 3ⁿ⁻¹ + 1 fits a₁ = 2 but gives a₂ = 4 instead of 5.

questions.s: Which of the following numbers is a term of the arithmetic sequence 2, 5, 8, 11, …?
questions.e: aₙ = 3n − 1, so every term leaves remainder 2 when divided by 3. 2024 = 3 × 675 − 1 is the 675th term. 2023 and 2026 leave remainder 1, and 2025 is a multiple of 3.

questions.s: A geometric sequence aₙ = a₁qⁿ⁻¹ has a₁ > 0 and 0 < q < 1. Which describes the sequence?
questions.e: All terms are positive and aₙ₊₁ = qaₙ < aₙ because q < 1, so the sequence is decreasing. It would be increasing only for a₁ > 0 with q > 1, and alternating only for q < 0.

questions.s: In a geometric sequence, a₃ = 2. What is the product a₁a₂a₃a₄a₅?
questions.e: a₁a₅ = a₂a₄ = a₃², so the product is a₃⁵ = 2⁵ = 32. Multiplying 5 × 2 instead of raising 2 to the fifth power gives 10.
1/(k(k + 1)) = 1/k − 1/(k + 1), so the sum telescopes to 1 − 1/(n + 1) = n/(n + 1). Setting n/(n + 1) = 9/10 gives n = 9. Choosing 10 matches the denominator n + 1, not n.

questions.s: A sequence has general term aₙ = 10 − 2n. What is |a₁| + |a₂| + … + |a₁₀|?
questions.e: The terms are 8, 6, 4, 2, 0, −2, −4, −6, −8, −10. The first five add to 20 and the absolute values of the last five add to 30, so the total is 50. The value −10 is the plain sum a₁ + … + a₁₀, which ignores the absolute values.

questions.s: Three positive numbers are inserted between 1 and 256 so that the five numbers form a geometric sequence. What is the product of the three inserted numbers?
questions.e: q⁴ = 256 and q > 0 give q = 4, so the inserted numbers are 4, 16, 64, with product 4096 (= 16³). Their sum is 84, which answers a different question.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 10 and common difference −2.5. Which is its first negative term?
questions.e: aₙ = 10 − 2.5(n − 1) is 0 at n = 5 and −2.5 at n = 6, so the first negative term is the 6th. The 5th term is exactly 0, which is not negative.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of an arithmetic sequence is Sₙ = 3n² + 2n. What is its common difference?
questions.e: a₁ = S₁ = 5 and a₂ = S₂ − S₁ = 16 − 5 = 11, so d = 6. In Sₙ = (d/2)n² + (a₁ − d/2)n the n² coefficient is d/2, so reading d = 3 directly off the formula is the trap; 5 is a₁.

questions.s: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 9 + 3 + 1 + 1/3 + …?
questions.e: a₁ = 9 and q = 1/3, so S = 9/(1 − 1/3) = 9 × 3/2 = 27/2. The value 13 is only the first three terms, and 18 uses q = 1/2.

questions.s: A sequence has general term aₙ = (2n − 1) + (1/2)ⁿ. Which expression gives the sum of its first n terms?
questions.e: Sum the two parts separately: 1 + 3 + … + (2n − 1) = n², and 1/2 + 1/4 + … + 1/2ⁿ = 1 − 1/2ⁿ. So Sₙ = n² + 1 − 1/2ⁿ. Check n = 2: S₂ = 3/2 + 13/4 = 19/4 = 4 + 1 − 1/4, whereas n² + 1/2ⁿ gives 17/4.

questions.s: Three positive numbers a, b, c form an arithmetic sequence with sum 15, and a + 1, b + 3, c + 9 form a geometric sequence. What is c?
questions.e: b = 5; write a = 5 − d, c = 5 + d. Then 8² = (6 − d)(14 + d) gives d² + 8d − 20 = 0, so d = 2 or d = −10. d = −10 makes c negative, so d = 2 and the numbers are 3, 5, 7: c = 7. The value 3 is a, not c.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 1 and a₈ = 15. What is the sum of its first 8 terms?
questions.e: S₈ = 8(a₁ + a₈)/2 = 8 × 16/2 = 64. Forgetting to divide by 2 gives 128.

questions.s: For a geometric sequence, S₁₀/S₅ = 33/32, where Sₙ is the sum of the first n terms. What is the common ratio?
questions.e: S₁₀ = S₅ + q⁵S₅, so S₁₀/S₅ = 1 + q⁵ = 33/32 and q⁵ = 1/32, giving q = 1/2. The value 1/32 is q⁵, not q, and q = 2 would give the ratio 33.

questions.s: Logs are stacked in rows: 20 logs in the bottom row, and each row above has one log fewer, up to a top row of 5 logs. How many logs are there altogether?
questions.e: The rows hold 20, 19, …, 5 logs: 16 rows, so the total is 16(20 + 5)/2 = 200. The value 210 is 1 + 2 + … + 20, as if the stack went up to a single log.

questions.s: The number x makes 2, x, 8 an arithmetic sequence, and the positive number y makes 2, y, 8 a geometric sequence. What is x − y?
questions.e: x = (2 + 8)/2 = 5 and y = √(2 × 8) = 4, so x − y = 1. Swapping the two means gives −1.

questions.s: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 1 and aₙ₊₁ = aₙ + 1/(n(n + 1)) for n ≥ 1. What is a₁₀?
questions.e: a₁₀ = 1 + Σ from k = 1 to 9 of (1/k − 1/(k + 1)) = 1 + (1 − 1/10) = 19/10. Summing up to k = 10 instead gives 21/11, and 9/10 forgets the starting value a₁ = 1.

questions.s: A geometric sequence with positive terms has a₁ + a₂ = 3 and a₃ + a₄ = 12. What is a₅ + a₆?
questions.e: (a₃ + a₄)/(a₁ + a₂) = q² = 4, so a₅ + a₆ = 12q² = 48. Adding the same amount each time (as if arithmetic) would give 21, and 24 multiplies by q = 2 instead of q².

questions.s: What is the 10th term of the arithmetic sequence 12, 7, 2, −3, …?
questions.e: a₁ = 12 and d = −5, so a₁₀ = 12 + 9 × (−5) = −33. Using 10d gives −38, and −28 is the 9th term.

questions.s: What is the sum of the first 8 terms of the geometric sequence 3, 6, 12, 24, …?
questions.e: a₁ = 3 and q = 2, so S₈ = 3(2⁸ − 1)/(2 − 1) = 3 × 255 = 765. The value 768 = 3 × 2⁸ forgets the − 1, and 381 is S₇.

questions.s: A sequence has general term aₙ = 2ⁿ − n. What is a₆?
questions.e: a₆ = 2⁶ − 6 = 64 − 6 = 58. Adding n instead of subtracting gives 70, and 27 is a₅.

questions.s: In an arithmetic sequence, a₂ = 5 and a₆ = 17. What is the common difference?
questions.e: a₆ − a₂ = 4d = 12, so d = 3. Dividing by 3 instead of 4 (counting terms, not gaps) gives 4, and 12 is the total change, not the difference per step.

questions.s: What is the sum of the infinite geometric series 2 + 2/5 + 2/25 + …?
questions.e: a₁ = 2 and q = 1/5, so S = 2/(1 − 1/5) = 2/(4/5) = 5/2. Using 1 + q gives 5/3, and 12/5 is only the first two terms.

questions.s: In any arithmetic sequence {aₙ}, which expression is always equal to a₂ + a₈?
questions.e: If m + n = p + q then aₘ + aₙ = aₚ + a_q; here 2 + 8 = 1 + 9, so a₂ + a₈ = a₁ + a₉ (= 2a₅). Adding the indices to get a₁₀ is a common mistake, and 2a₄ would need 4 + 4 = 10.

questions.s: What is the value of 2 + 4 + 6 + … + 100?
questions.e: There are 50 terms, so the sum is 50(2 + 100)/2 = 2550 (or 2 × (1 + … + 50) = 2 × 1275). 5050 is the sum of all integers from 1 to 100.

questions.s: A geometric sequence has a₁ = 1/4 and common ratio 2. Which term is equal to 64?
questions.e: aₙ = (1/4) × 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 2ⁿ⁻³, and 2ⁿ⁻³ = 64 = 2⁶ gives n = 9. Solving 2ⁿ⁻¹ = 64 and forgetting the factor 1/4 gives the 7th term.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ = 20 and common difference −4. For which n is the sum of the first n terms equal to 0?
questions.e: Sₙ = n[2 × 20 + (n − 1)(−4)]/2 = n(44 − 4n)/2 = 0 gives n = 11 (n ≠ 0). The value 6 is where the terms themselves reach 0 (a₆ = 0), which is different from the sum being 0.

questions.s: In an arithmetic sequence, a₅ = 8. What is the sum of the first 9 terms?
questions.e: S₉ = 9(a₁ + a₉)/2 and a₁ + a₉ = 2a₅ = 16, so S₉ = 9 × 8 = 72. Forgetting to halve 9 × 16 gives 144.

questions.s: A geometric sequence has a₁ = 4 and a₄ = −32. What is the sum of its first 5 terms?
questions.e: q³ = −32/4 = −8, so q = −2 and the terms are 4, −8, 16, −32, 64, with sum 44. By formula 4(1 − (−2)⁵)/(1 − (−2)) = 4 × 33/3 = 44; forgetting to divide by 3 gives 132, and using q = 2 gives 124.

questions.s: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 1 and aₙ₊₁ = aₙ + n for n ≥ 1. What is a₂₀?
questions.e: a₂₀ = 1 + (1 + 2 + … + 19) = 1 + 190 = 191 (in general aₙ = 1 + n(n − 1)/2). Adding up to 20 instead of 19 gives 211, and 190 forgets a₁ = 1.
1/(k(k − 1)) = 1/(k − 1) − 1/k, so the sum from k = 2 to 10 telescopes to 1 − 1/10 = 9/10. Ending at 1/11 instead of 1/10 gives 10/11.

questions.s: A geometric sequence with positive terms has a₂ = 2 and a₄ = 8. What is the sum of its first 6 terms?
questions.e: q² = 8/2 = 4, so q = 2 and a₁ = 1; then S₆ = 2⁶ − 1 = 63. The value 64 = 2⁶ forgets the − 1, and 31 is S₅.

questions.s: Kwame runs 2 km on day 1 and increases his distance by 0.5 km each day. On which day does he first run 10 km?
questions.e: 2 + 0.5(n − 1) = 10 gives n − 1 = 16, so n = 17. The answer 16th counts the number of increases (8/0.5) but forgets that day 1 already has 2 km.

questions.s: The sum of the first n terms of a sequence is Sₙ = n² + 4n. What is its general term aₙ?
questions.e: For n ≥ 2, aₙ = Sₙ − Sₙ₋₁ = (n² + 4n) − ((n − 1)² + 4(n − 1)) = 2n + 3, and a₁ = S₁ = 5 also fits. 2n + 5 gives a₁ = 7, which does not match S₁ = 5.

questions.s: The real numbers 1, x, y, 27 (in this order) form a geometric sequence. What is x + y?
questions.e: q³ = 27 gives q = 3, so x = 3 and y = 9, and x + y = 12. The value 27 is the product xy, and 9 is only y.

questions.s: A square has side 4 cm. Joining the midpoints of its sides gives a second square; joining the midpoints of that square gives a third, and so on forever. What is the total area of all the squares?
questions.e: Each new square has half the area of the one before (16, 8, 4, …), so the total is 16/(1 − 1/2) = 32 cm². Taking the side ratio as 1/2 (so an area ratio of 1/4) gives 64/3 cm², and 28 cm² stops after three squares.

questions.s: Several numbers are inserted between 1 and 25 so that together they form an arithmetic sequence with common difference 3. What is the sum of the inserted numbers?
questions.e: The sequence is 1, 4, 7, …, 25, so the inserted numbers are 4, 7, …, 22: seven numbers with sum 7(4 + 22)/2 = 91. The value 117 is the sum of all nine terms including 1 and 25.

questions.s: A sequence is defined by a₁ = 3, a₂ = 6 and aₙ₊₂ = aₙ₊₁ − aₙ for n ≥ 1. What is a₁₀₀?
questions.e: The terms are 3, 6, 3, −3, −6, −3, 3, 6, …, repeating every 6 terms. Since 100 = 6 × 16 + 4, a₁₀₀ = a₄ = −3. Assuming a period of 3 instead of 6 gives a₁ = 3.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence has a₁ > 0 and S₄ = S₉, where Sₙ is the sum of the first n terms. For which n is Sₙ largest?
questions.e: S₉ − S₄ = a₅ + a₆ + a₇ + a₈ + a₉ = 5a₇ = 0, so a₇ = 0 and d < 0. The terms are positive up to a₆, so S₆ = S₇ is the maximum. Answering 6 only forgets that adding a₇ = 0 leaves the sum unchanged.

questions.s: What is the value of the infinite sum 1/2 + 2/4 + 3/8 + 4/16 + … + n/2ⁿ + …?
questions.e: Let S = Σ n/2ⁿ. Then S − S/2 = 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … = 1, so S/2 = 1 and S = 2. The value 1 is the sum of the geometric series alone, before dividing by 1/2.

questions.s: An arithmetic sequence {aₙ} has common difference 2, and a₁, a₂, a₄ form a geometric sequence. What is 1/(a₁a₂) + 1/(a₂a₃) + … + 1/(a₁₀a₁₁)?
questions.e: (a₁ + 2)² = a₁(a₁ + 6) gives a₁ = 2, so aₙ = 2n and 1/(aₖaₖ₊₁) = ¼[1/k − 1/(k + 1)]. The sum is ¼(1 − 1/11) = 5/22. Forgetting the factor ¼ gives 10/11.

questions.s: A sequence satisfies a₁ = 2 and aₙ₊₁ = 2aₙ + 2ⁿ⁺¹ for n ≥ 1. What is a₅?
questions.e: Divide by 2ⁿ⁺¹: aₙ₊₁/2ⁿ⁺¹ = aₙ/2ⁿ + 1, so {aₙ/2ⁿ} is arithmetic with first term 1 and difference 1. Hence aₙ = n · 2ⁿ and a₅ = 5 × 32 = 160. The value 80 = 5 × 2⁴ uses the wrong power of 2.

questions.s: What is the value of 3 + 7 + 11 + … + 39?
questions.e: The common difference is 4, so there are (39 − 3)/4 + 1 = 10 terms and the sum is 10(3 + 39)/2 = 210. Forgetting the + 1 when counting terms gives 9 × 42/2 = 189, and forgetting to halve gives 420.

questions.s: Let f(x) = x³. What is the value of lim(Δx→0) [f(2 + Δx) − f(2)]/Δx?
questions.e: The limit is the definition of f′(2). Since f′(x) = 3x², f′(2) = 3 × 4 = 12. The value 8 is f(2), not the derivative, and 6 comes from writing 3x instead of 3x².

questions.s: If f′(x₀) = 3, what is the value of lim(h→0) [f(x₀ + 2h) − f(x₀)]/h?
questions.e: Write the quotient as 2 × [f(x₀ + 2h) − f(x₀)]/(2h); as h → 0 the bracket tends to f′(x₀) = 3, so the limit is 2 × 3 = 6. Answering 3 ignores that the increment is 2h while the denominator is only h; 3/2 divides by 2 instead of multiplying.

questions.s: If f′(x₀) = 4, what is the value of lim(h→0) [f(x₀ − h) − f(x₀)]/h?
questions.e: Put k = −h: the expression becomes −[f(x₀ + k) − f(x₀)]/k, which tends to −f′(x₀) = −4. The answer 4 overlooks that the increment in x is −h while the denominator is +h.

questions.s: If f′(x₀) = 2, what is the value of lim(h→0) [f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀ − h)]/h?
questions.e: Split the numerator: [f(x₀ + h) − f(x₀)]/h + [f(x₀) − f(x₀ − h)]/h. Each part tends to f′(x₀) = 2, so the limit is 4. The answer 2 forgets that the total change in x is 2h, not h.

questions.s: What is the average rate of change of f(x) = x² + 1 on the interval [1, 3]?
questions.e: Average rate of change = [f(3) − f(1)]/(3 − 1) = (10 − 2)/2 = 4. The value 8 is the change in f without dividing by the length of the interval; 2 and 6 are the instantaneous rates f′(1) and f′(3).

questions.s: For a differentiable function y = f(x), what is the geometric meaning of f′(x₀)?
o: The y-intercept of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x = x₀
The value of f(x) at x = x₀ divided by x₀
The slope of the tangent line to y = f(x) at x = x₀
The average rate of change of f(x) from x = 0 to x = x₀
questions.e: f′(x₀) is the limit of the slopes of secant lines through (x₀, f(x₀)), which is the slope of the tangent line at that point. The average rate of change from 0 to x₀ is the slope of one particular secant, not the tangent, and the y-intercept of the tangent is f(x₀) − x₀f′(x₀), not f′(x₀).

questions.s: An object moves along a straight line with displacement s(t) = 3t² − 2t (s in metres, t in seconds). What is its instantaneous velocity at t = 2 s?
questions.e: Velocity is the derivative of displacement: v(t) = s′(t) = 6t − 2, so v(2) = 10 m/s. The value 8 is the displacement s(2) = 12 − 4, and 4 m/s is the average velocity over the first 2 s.

questions.s: A particle moves along a line with position s(t) = t³ − 6t² + 9t (t > 0, SI units). At which times is the particle momentarily at rest?
questions.e: At rest means v = s′(t) = 0: 3t² − 12t + 9 = 3(t − 1)(t − 3) = 0, so t = 1 s or t = 3 s. Choosing t = 3 s only comes from solving s(t) = t(t − 3)² = 0, which gives the times at the origin, not at rest.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = x⁵?
questions.e: By the power rule (xⁿ)′ = nxⁿ⁻¹, so y′ = 5x⁴. The option x⁶/6 is an antiderivative, not a derivative, and 5x⁵ forgets to lower the power by one.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = √x (x > 0)?
questions.e: Write √x = x^(1/2); the power rule gives (1/2)x^(−1/2) = 1/(2√x). The option √x/2 keeps the original power instead of reducing it by one, and the negative option confuses √x with 1/√x.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = 1/x²?
questions.e: Write 1/x² = x⁻²; then y′ = −2x⁻³ = −2/x³. The option 2/x³ drops the minus sign from the exponent, and −2/x lowers the power in the wrong direction.

questions.s: Which of the following derivative formulas is correct?
questions.e: The standard results are (sin x)′ = cos x, (cos x)′ = −sin x, (eˣ)′ = eˣ and (ln x)′ = 1/x (x > 0). The formula x·eˣ⁻¹ wrongly applies the power rule to an exponential function, and the two trigonometric options have the minus sign in the wrong place.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = 2ˣ?
questions.e: For aˣ with a > 0, (aˣ)′ = aˣ ln a, so y′ = 2ˣ ln 2. The option x·2ˣ⁻¹ treats the exponential as a power function, and 2ˣ alone is correct only for base e.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = log₃ x (x > 0)?
questions.e: Since log₃ x = ln x / ln 3, y′ = 1/(x ln 3). The option 1/x is the derivative of ln x only, and ln 3/x puts ln 3 in the numerator instead of the denominator.

questions.s: If f(x) = sin x, what is the value of f′(π/3)?
questions.e: f′(x) = cos x, so f′(π/3) = cos(π/3) = 1/2. The value √3/2 is sin(π/3), the function value rather than the derivative.

questions.s: If f(x) = cos x, what is the value of f′(π/6)?
questions.e: f′(x) = −sin x, so f′(π/6) = −sin(π/6) = −1/2. Forgetting the minus sign gives 1/2, and √3/2 is just cos(π/6).

questions.s: If f(x) = π², what is f′(x)?
questions.e: π² is a constant (about 9.87), and the derivative of any constant is 0. Writing 2π treats π as the variable, which it is not.

questions.s: If f(x) = x³ − 2x² + 5x − 1, what is the value of f′(1)?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 4x + 5, so f′(1) = 3 − 4 + 5 = 4. The value 3 is f(1), and 12 comes from adding 3 + 4 + 5 after losing the minus sign.

questions.s: What is the derivative of f(x) = x²eˣ?
questions.e: Product rule: f′(x) = (x²)′eˣ + x²(eˣ)′ = 2x eˣ + x²eˣ = (x² + 2x)eˣ. The option 2x eˣ differentiates only the first factor and drops the term x²eˣ.

questions.s: If f(x) = x ln x (x > 0), what is the value of f′(e)?
questions.e: Product rule: f′(x) = ln x + x·(1/x) = ln x + 1, so f′(e) = 1 + 1 = 2. The answer 1 keeps only one term of the product rule (either ln e or x·1/x).

questions.s: If f(x) = (x + 1)/(x − 1), what is the value of f′(2)?
questions.e: Quotient rule: f′(x) = [(x − 1) − (x + 1)]/(x − 1)² = −2/(x − 1)², so f′(2) = −2/1 = −2. Getting +2 comes from subtracting the numerator terms in the wrong order.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = sin x / x (x ≠ 0)?
questions.e: Quotient rule: y′ = [(sin x)′·x − sin x·(x)′]/x² = (x cos x − sin x)/x². The option (sin x − x cos x)/x² reverses the order of the subtraction, which changes the sign, and cos x simply divides the derivatives.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = (2x + 1)⁵?
questions.e: Chain rule: y′ = 5(2x + 1)⁴ × (2x + 1)′ = 5(2x + 1)⁴ × 2 = 10(2x + 1)⁴. The option 5(2x + 1)⁴ forgets to multiply by the inner derivative 2.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = e⁻³ˣ?
questions.e: Chain rule with u = −3x: y′ = eᵘ·u′ = −3e⁻³ˣ. Writing e⁻³ˣ forgets the inner derivative, and 3e⁻³ˣ loses its minus sign.

questions.s: If y = ln(2x − 1), what is the value of y′ at x = 1?
questions.e: Chain rule: y′ = 2/(2x − 1), so at x = 1, y′ = 2/1 = 2. The answer 1 forgets the inner derivative 2 and uses 1/(2x − 1).

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent line to y = x² at the point (1, 1)?
questions.e: y′ = 2x, so the slope at x = 1 is 2 and the tangent is y − 1 = 2(x − 1), i.e. y = 2x − 1. The line y = 2x has the right slope but does not pass through (1, 1).

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent line to the curve y = x³ − 2x at the point where x = 1?
questions.e: At x = 1, y = 1 − 2 = −1 and y′ = 3x² − 2 = 1, so the tangent is y + 1 = 1·(x − 1), i.e. y = x − 2. The option y = 3x − 4 uses slope 3 from differentiating only the x³ term.

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent line to y = eˣ at the point where x = 0?
questions.e: At x = 0 the point is (0, 1) and the slope is e⁰ = 1, so the tangent is y = x + 1. The line y = x has the correct slope but misses the point (0, 1).

questions.s: The tangent line to y = ln x at the point (e, 1) also passes through which of the following points?
questions.e: The slope is 1/x = 1/e, so the tangent is y − 1 = (x − e)/e, which simplifies to y = x/e and passes through the origin. The point (0, −1) lies on the tangent at (1, 0), which is y = x − 1, not the tangent at (e, 1).

questions.s: What is the angle of inclination of the tangent line to y = x³/3 − 2x at the point where x = 1?
questions.e: y′ = x² − 2, so the slope at x = 1 is −1. An angle of inclination α in [0, π) with tan α = −1 is α = 3π/4. Answering π/4 ignores the negative sign of the slope.

questions.s: Two lines pass through the point P(2, 3) and are tangent to the parabola y = x². What is the sum of their slopes?
questions.e: The tangent at (a, a²) is y = 2ax − a². It passes through (2, 3) when 3 = 4a − a², i.e. a² − 4a + 3 = 0, so a = 1 or a = 3. The slopes are 2a = 2 and 6, with sum 8. The answer 4 is the sum of the tangency x-coordinates a, not of the slopes 2a.

questions.s: The tangent to the curve y = x² − x at some point is parallel to the line y = 3x + 1. What is the equation of this tangent?
questions.e: Parallel means slope 3: y′ = 2x − 1 = 3 gives x = 2 and y = 4 − 2 = 2. The tangent is y − 2 = 3(x − 2), i.e. y = 3x − 4. The option y = 3x + 4 comes from a sign error when expanding 3(x − 2).

questions.s: The tangent to y = x ln x at a point P is perpendicular to the line x + 2y = 0. What is the equation of this tangent?
questions.e: The line x + 2y = 0 has slope −1/2, so the tangent has slope 2. y′ = ln x + 1 = 2 gives x = e and y = e ln e = e, so P = (e, e) and the tangent is y − e = 2(x − e), i.e. y = 2x − e. The option y = 2x − 1 uses the point x = 1, where the slope is only 1.

questions.s: A line through the origin is tangent to the curve y = eˣ. What is the slope of this line?
questions.e: The tangent at (a, eᵃ) is y − eᵃ = eᵃ(x − a). Passing through (0, 0) gives −eᵃ = −aeᵃ, so a = 1 and the slope is e¹ = e. The answer 1 is the slope at x = 0, but the tangent there, y = x + 1, does not pass through the origin.

questions.s: The tangent line to the curve y = 1/x at the point (1, 1) forms a triangle with the two coordinate axes. What is the area of this triangle?
questions.e: y′ = −1/x² gives slope −1 at x = 1, so the tangent is y = −x + 2. Its intercepts are (2, 0) and (0, 2), so the area is ½ × 2 × 2 = 2. The answer 4 forgets the factor ½ for a triangle.

questions.s: The tangent line to f(x) = x³ + ax + b at the point where x = 1 is y = 2x + 1. What is the value of ab?
questions.e: The point is (1, 3), so f(1) = 1 + a + b = 3, and the slope gives f′(1) = 3 + a = 2. Hence a = −1 and b = 3, so ab = −3. The options −1 and 3 are a and b themselves, not their product.

questions.s: What is the slope of the tangent line to y = 4/x at the point where x = 2?
questions.e: y′ = −4/x², so at x = 2 the slope is −4/4 = −1. The value 2 is the y-coordinate of the point, and −2 comes from using −4/x instead of −4/x².

questions.s: Which statement about a function f is true?
o: If f′(x₀) = 0, then f has an extremum at x = x₀.
If differentiable f has a local maximum at x = x₀, then f′(x₀) = 0.
If f is increasing on (a, b), then f′(x) > 0 for every x in (a, b).
A local maximum value of f is always larger than any local minimum value of f.
questions.e: At an interior local extremum of a differentiable function the tangent is horizontal, so f′(x₀) = 0. The converse fails: f(x) = x³ has f′(0) = 0 but no extremum there, and the same function is increasing although f′(0) = 0. A local maximum can also be smaller than a local minimum elsewhere on the graph.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = x² − 4x + 3 decreasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = 2x − 4 < 0 when x < 2, so f is decreasing on (−∞, 2). The interval (1, 3) is where f(x) < 0, which is a different question from where f is decreasing.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = x³ − 3x decreasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 3(x − 1)(x + 1) < 0 when −1 < x < 1, so f decreases on (−1, 1). The interval (0, √3) is where f(x) < 0, which is about the sign of f, not of f′.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = x − ln x increasing?
questions.e: The domain is x > 0 and f′(x) = 1 − 1/x = (x − 1)/x > 0 when x > 1, so f increases on (1, +∞). On (0, 1) the derivative is negative, so (0, +∞) is too large.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = xeˣ decreasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ + xeˣ = (x + 1)eˣ, and eˣ > 0, so f′(x) < 0 exactly when x < −1. The interval (−∞, 0) is where f(x) < 0, not where f decreases.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ − ax is increasing on [1, +∞). What is the range of the real number a?
questions.e: We need f′(x) = 3x² − a ≥ 0 for all x ≥ 1, i.e. a ≤ 3x² for all x ≥ 1. The smallest value of 3x² there is 3, so a ≤ 3. The endpoint a = 3 is allowed because f′(x) = 3x² − 3 is zero only at x = 1, so the strict option a < 3 is too narrow.

questions.s: The function f(x) = ax − ln x is decreasing on the interval (1, 2). What is the range of a?
questions.e: We need f′(x) = a − 1/x ≤ 0, i.e. a ≤ 1/x for every x in (1, 2). On this interval 1/x takes all values in (1/2, 1), so a ≤ 1/2. The answer a ≤ 1 only works near x = 1; for a = 1, f′(x) = 1 − 1/x > 0 on (1, 2).

questions.s: What are the increasing intervals of f(x) = x³/3 − x² − 3x?
questions.e: f′(x) = x² − 2x − 3 = (x − 3)(x + 1) > 0 when x < −1 or x > 3. The interval (−1, 3) is where f decreases, and (−∞, −3) and (1, +∞) come from factorising with the wrong signs.

questions.s: On the interval (0, π), where is f(x) = x − 2 sin x increasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = 1 − 2 cos x > 0 means cos x < 1/2, which on (0, π) holds for π/3 < x < π. The interval (0, π/3) is where f′(x) < 0, and π/6 would come from confusing cos x = 1/2 with sin x = 1/2.

questions.s: Which of the following functions is increasing on (0, +∞)?
questions.e: For y = xeˣ, y′ = (x + 1)eˣ > 0 for all x > 0. The others decrease near 0: (x ln x)′ = ln x + 1 < 0 on (0, 1/e), (x³ − x)′ = 3x² − 1 < 0 on (0, 1/√3), and (eˣ − 2x)′ = eˣ − 2 < 0 on (0, ln 2).

questions.s: A function f satisfies f′(x) > 0 for every x in (0, 2). Which of the following must be true?
questions.e: A positive derivative on (0, 2) means f is increasing there, so 1.5 > 0.5 gives f(1.5) > f(0.5). Nothing forces f(1.5) > 0: f(x) = x − 10 is increasing but negative on the whole interval.

questions.s: For a function f, the derivative satisfies f′(x) < 0 for x < −1, f′(x) > 0 for −1 < x < 2, and f′(x) < 0 for x > 2. Which statement is correct?
o: f has a local minimum at x = −1 and a local maximum at x = 2
f has a local maximum at x = −1 and a local minimum at x = 2
f has local maxima at both x = −1 and x = 2
f has local minima at both x = −1 and x = 2
questions.e: At x = −1 the function changes from decreasing to increasing, which gives a local minimum; at x = 2 it changes from increasing to decreasing, which gives a local maximum. The swapped option reads the sign pattern of f′ as if it were the shape of f itself.

questions.s: What is the local maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 1?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x = 3x(x − 2) = 0 at x = 0 and x = 2. f′ changes from + to − at x = 0, so the local maximum value is f(0) = 1; f(2) = −3 is the local minimum value. The answer 0 gives the x-coordinate instead of the value.

questions.s: What is the local minimum value of f(x) = x³ − 12x?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 12 = 3(x − 2)(x + 2) = 0 at x = ±2. f′ changes from − to + at x = 2, so the local minimum value is f(2) = 8 − 24 = −16; f(−2) = 16 is the local maximum. The answer 2 is the position of the minimum, not its value.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ + ax² + 3x − 9 has an extremum at x = −3. What is the value of a?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² + 2ax + 3, and an extremum requires f′(−3) = 27 − 6a + 3 = 0, so a = 5. Check: f′(x) = 3x² + 10x + 3 = (3x + 1)(x + 3) does change sign at x = −3. Using f(−3) = 0 instead of f′(−3) = 0 is the usual mistake.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ + ax² + bx has a local extremum with value −2 at x = 1. What is the value of a + b?
questions.e: Two conditions: f′(1) = 3 + 2a + b = 0 and f(1) = 1 + a + b = −2. Subtracting gives 2 + a = 2, so a = 0 and b = −3, hence a + b = −3. Check: f(x) = x³ − 3x has a local minimum −2 at x = 1. Using only one of the two conditions leaves a and b undetermined.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = x − 2 ln x?
questions.e: For x > 0, f′(x) = 1 − 2/x = 0 at x = 2; f decreases on (0, 2) and increases on (2, +∞), so the minimum is f(2) = 2 − 2 ln 2. The value 1 is f(1), which is not the lowest point, and 2 ln 2 − 2 has the sign reversed.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = eˣ − x?
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ − 1 = 0 at x = 0, with f′ < 0 for x < 0 and f′ > 0 for x > 0, so the minimum is f(0) = 1 − 0 = 1. The value e − 1 is f(1), which is larger.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = xeˣ?
questions.e: f′(x) = (x + 1)eˣ = 0 at x = −1, where f′ changes from − to +. The minimum is f(−1) = −e⁻¹ = −1/e. The value −1 is the x-coordinate of the minimum point, not the minimum value.

questions.s: How many extreme points (local maxima and minima) does f(x) = x³ + x have?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² + 1 > 0 for every x, so f is increasing on the whole real line and has no extreme points. Answering 1 or 2 assumes every cubic has turning points, which is false here because f′ never changes sign.

questions.s: The equation x³ − 3x + a = 0 has three distinct real roots. What is the range of a?
questions.e: Let f(x) = x³ − 3x + a; f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 at x = ±1. Three distinct zeros need the local maximum f(−1) = 2 + a > 0 and the local minimum f(1) = −2 + a < 0, so −2 < a < 2. The option −1 < a < 1 uses the critical x-values instead of the extreme values.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ − ax² + 3x has a local maximum and also a local minimum. What is the range of a?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 2ax + 3 must have two distinct real roots, so Δ = 4a² − 36 > 0, giving a < −3 or a > 3. With a = ±3 the root is double and f′ does not change sign, so the option with ≤ and ≥ is wrong; a > 3 alone forgets the negative branch.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x on the closed interval [0, 2]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 at x = 1 in the interval. Compare f(0) = 0, f(1) = −2 and f(2) = 8 − 6 = 2; the largest is 2, at the endpoint. Answering 0 checks only the critical point and the left endpoint and misses the right endpoint.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = 2x³ − 6x² + 1 on the closed interval [−1, 1]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 6x² − 12x = 6x(x − 2), so the only critical point in [−1, 1] is x = 0. Compare f(−1) = −2 − 6 + 1 = −7, f(0) = 1 and f(1) = −3; the minimum is −7. The value −3 comes from checking only the right endpoint.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x + 2 cos x on the interval [0, π/2]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 1 − 2 sin x = 0 at x = π/6, with f′ > 0 before and f′ < 0 after, so x = π/6 gives the maximum f(π/6) = π/6 + 2·(√3/2) = π/6 + √3 (about 2.25). It exceeds f(0) = 2 and f(π/2) = π/2. The option π/3 + 1 uses the wrong critical point x = π/3.

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = ln x − x on the interval [1/e, e]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 1/x − 1 = 0 at x = 1, which gives the maximum f(1) = −1. The minimum is at an endpoint: f(1/e) = −1 − 1/e (about −1.37) and f(e) = 1 − e (about −1.72), so the minimum is 1 − e. The answer −1 is the maximum value, not the minimum.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x(3 − x)² on the interval [0, 3]?
questions.e: f′(x) = (3 − x)² − 2x(3 − x) = (3 − x)(3 − 3x) = 3(3 − x)(1 − x), so the critical point inside is x = 1 with f(1) = 1 × 4 = 4. At the endpoints f(0) = f(3) = 0, so the maximum is 4. The value 3 is just the endpoint x = 3.

questions.s: A square sheet of side 6 cm has a square of side x cm cut from each corner, and the sides are folded up to make an open box. For which x is the volume of the box largest?
questions.e: V(x) = x(6 − 2x)² for 0 < x < 3. V′(x) = (6 − 2x)² − 4x(6 − 2x) = (6 − 2x)(6 − 6x) = 0 at x = 1 (x = 3 gives zero volume), and V changes from increasing to decreasing there, so the maximum volume is V(1) = 16 cm³. For comparison, V(3/2) = 3/2 × 9 = 13.5 cm³ and V(2) = 8 cm³, both smaller than 16 cm³.

questions.s: A rectangle has one side on the x-axis and its two upper vertices on the parabola y = 3 − x². What is the largest possible area of the rectangle?
questions.e: With upper vertices (±a, 3 − a²), 0 < a < √3, the area is A(a) = 2a(3 − a²) = 6a − 2a³. A′(a) = 6 − 6a² = 0 gives a = 1, where A changes from increasing to decreasing, so the maximum area is 2 × 1 × 2 = 4. Using width a instead of 2a would halve the area function and lead to a different value.

questions.s: A factory's profit (in thousands of yuan) from producing x thousand units is P(x) = −x³/3 + 81x − 234 for 0 < x < 15. For which x is the profit largest?
questions.e: P′(x) = −x² + 81 = 0 at x = 9 in (0, 15). P′ > 0 for x < 9 and P′ < 0 for x > 9, so x = 9 gives the maximum profit. The value 81 is x² at that point, not x itself.

questions.s: An open-top box with a square base must have volume 32 cm³. What is the smallest possible total area of its base and four sides?
questions.e: With base side x and height h, x²h = 32 so h = 32/x², and the area is S = x² + 4xh = x² + 128/x. S′ = 2x − 128/x² = 0 gives x³ = 64, x = 4 and h = 2, so S = 16 + 32 = 48 cm². Including a lid (2x² instead of x²) would change the function and give a different answer.

questions.s: Which point on the parabola y = x² is closest to the line y = 2x − 4?
questions.e: The closest point is where the tangent is parallel to the line, so y′ = 2x = 2 and x = 1, giving (1, 1); the distance is |2 − 1 − 4|/√5 = 3/√5. The point (2, 4) lies on the parabola where the slope is 4, so its tangent is not parallel to the line.

questions.s: f(x) is continuous on the closed interval [a, b]. Which statement must be true?
o: Its maximum value is always one of its local maximum values.
Its maximum value must occur at a point where f′(x) = 0.
It can have at most one local maximum point in (a, b).
It must attain a maximum value and a minimum value.
questions.e: A continuous function on a closed interval always attains a maximum value and a minimum value. The maximum may occur at an endpoint, where it need not be a local maximum and f′ need not be 0; for example f(x) = x on [0, 1] has its maximum 1 at x = 1. A function such as sin x on [0, 4π] has several local maxima.

questions.s: What is the sum of the local maximum value and the local minimum value of f(x) = 2x³ − 3x² − 12x + 5?
questions.e: f′(x) = 6x² − 6x − 12 = 6(x − 2)(x + 1). The local maximum is f(−1) = −2 − 3 + 12 + 5 = 12 and the local minimum is f(2) = 16 − 12 − 24 + 5 = −15, so the sum is −3. The value 27 is their difference, not their sum.

questions.s: The derivative of a function f is f′(x) = (x − 1)²(x − 2). How many extreme points does f have?
questions.e: f′(x) = 0 at x = 1 and x = 2. Around x = 1 the factor (x − 1)² does not change sign, so f′ stays negative and x = 1 is not an extreme point; at x = 2, f′ changes from − to +, giving one local minimum. Answering 2 counts every zero of f′ as an extremum.

questions.s: What is the local maximum value of f(x) = (x² − 3)eˣ?
questions.e: f′(x) = 2xeˣ + (x² − 3)eˣ = (x² + 2x − 3)eˣ = (x + 3)(x − 1)eˣ. f′ changes from + to − at x = −3, so the local maximum value is f(−3) = 6e⁻³. The value −2e is f(1), the local minimum.

questions.s: For x > 0, what is the minimum value of f(x) = x + 4/x?
questions.e: f′(x) = 1 − 4/x² = 0 at x = 2 (x > 0), with f′ < 0 on (0, 2) and f′ > 0 after, so the minimum is f(2) = 2 + 2 = 4. The value 2 is where the minimum occurs, and 5 is f(1).

questions.s: Let f(x) = eˣ − x − 1. By studying the minimum of f, which statement can be proved?
o: eˣ ≤ x + 1 for all real x
eˣ > x + 1 for all real x
eˣ ≥ x + 1 for all real x
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ − 1 is negative for x < 0 and positive for x > 0, so f has its minimum f(0) = 0. Hence f(x) ≥ 0, i.e. eˣ ≥ x + 1 for every real x. The strict inequality fails at x = 0, where both sides equal 1.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = 3x² − 5x + 2?
questions.e: Differentiate term by term: (3x²)′ = 6x, (−5x)′ = −5 and the constant 2 gives 0, so y′ = 6x − 5. The option 6x + 2 keeps the constant term, whose derivative is 0.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = eˣ + ln x (x > 0)?
questions.e: Using (eˣ)′ = eˣ and (ln x)′ = 1/x with the sum rule, y′ = eˣ + 1/x. The option x·eˣ⁻¹ + 1/x wrongly treats eˣ as a power of x.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = x sin x?
questions.e: Product rule: y′ = (x)′ sin x + x (sin x)′ = sin x + x cos x. The option cos x multiplies the derivatives of the two factors, which is not the product rule, and x cos x drops the term from differentiating x.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = eˣ/x (x ≠ 0)?
questions.e: Quotient rule: y′ = (eˣ·x − eˣ·1)/x² = (x − 1)eˣ/x². Reversing the order of subtraction in the numerator gives (1 − x)eˣ/x², which has the wrong sign.

questions.s: If y = sin(2x + π/3), what is the value of y′ at x = 0?
questions.e: Chain rule: y′ = 2cos(2x + π/3), so at x = 0, y′ = 2cos(π/3) = 2 × 1/2 = 1. Forgetting the inner factor 2 gives 1/2, and √3 comes from using sin instead of cos.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = cos² x?
questions.e: Chain rule with u = cos x: y′ = 2cos x·(cos x)′ = −2 sin x cos x = −sin 2x. The option sin 2x forgets that (cos x)′ = −sin x, and 2cos x forgets the inner derivative completely.

questions.s: At which x-coordinate does the tangent to y = ln x have slope 2?
questions.e: y′ = 1/x = 2 gives x = 1/2. The answer 2 sets x itself equal to the slope instead of solving 1/x = 2.

questions.s: At which points of the curve y = x³ + 1 does the tangent have slope 3?
questions.e: y′ = 3x² = 3 gives x² = 1, so x = 1 or x = −1, and the points are (1, 2) and (−1, 0). Taking only x = 1 forgets the negative square root.

questions.s: How many lines through the point (1, 0) are tangent to the curve y = x³?
questions.e: The tangent at (a, a³) is y = 3a²x − 2a³. It passes through (1, 0) when 3a² − 2a³ = a²(3 − 2a) = 0, so a = 0 or a = 3/2, giving the lines y = 0 and y = (27/4)x − 27/4. Answering 1 misses the tangent y = 0 at the origin, which also passes through (1, 0).

questions.s: The tangent to the curve y = ax³ at x = 1 has slope 6. What is the value of a?
questions.e: y′ = 3ax², so at x = 1 the slope is 3a = 6, giving a = 2. The answer 6 forgets the factor 3 from the power rule.

questions.s: Which statement about f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 3x is correct?
o: f has a local maximum at x = 1
f has a local minimum at x = 1
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x + 3 = 3(x − 1)² ≥ 0, with equality only at x = 1, so f is increasing on the whole real line. Since f′ does not change sign at x = 1, there is no local maximum or minimum there even though f′(1) = 0.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x² − a ln x is increasing on (1, +∞). What is the range of a?
questions.e: We need f′(x) = 2x − a/x ≥ 0 for x > 1, i.e. a ≤ 2x² for all x > 1. The values of 2x² there are all greater than 2, so a ≤ 2. The endpoint a = 2 works because f′(x) = 2x − 2/x > 0 for x > 1, so a < 2 is too strict.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ + ax² + x is increasing on the whole real line. What is the range of a?
questions.e: We need f′(x) = 3x² + 2ax + 1 ≥ 0 for all x, so Δ = 4a² − 12 ≤ 0, i.e. a² ≤ 3 and −√3 ≤ a ≤ √3. At a = ±√3 the derivative is a perfect square that is zero at one point only, so f is still increasing; the strict option leaves out these values.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = ln x − x²/2 increasing?
questions.e: The domain is x > 0, and f′(x) = 1/x − x = (1 − x²)/x > 0 when 0 < x < 1. The interval (−1, 1) ignores the domain of ln x, and (1, +∞) is where f decreases.

questions.s: The velocity of a car is v(t) = t² − 4t (v in m/s, t in s). What is its acceleration at t = 3 s?
questions.e: Acceleration is the derivative of velocity: a(t) = v′(t) = 2t − 4, so a(3) = 2 m/s². The value −3 is the velocity v(3) = 9 − 12, not the acceleration.

questions.s: The volume of water in a tank is V(t) = 100 + 6t − t² litres after t minutes. At what rate is the volume changing at t = 2 min?
questions.e: The rate of change is V′(t) = 6 − 2t, so V′(2) = 2 L/min. The value 108 is the volume V(2) = 100 + 12 − 4, not its rate of change.

questions.s: What are the maximum and minimum values of f(x) = x³ − 3x² on the closed interval [−1, 3]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x = 3x(x − 2) = 0 at x = 0 and x = 2. Comparing f(−1) = −4, f(0) = 0, f(2) = −4 and f(3) = 0 gives maximum 0 and minimum −4. Answers using 2 or −2 confuse the critical x-values with function values.

questions.s: A closed cylindrical tank must hold a volume of 16π m³. What is the smallest possible total surface area?
questions.e: With radius r, πr²h = 16π gives h = 16/r², so S = 2πr² + 2πrh = 2πr² + 32π/r. S′ = 4πr − 32π/r² = 0 gives r³ = 8, r = 2 and h = 4, so S = 8π + 16π = 24π m². Forgetting one of the two circular ends leads to a different function and a wrong value.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x − sin x on the interval [0, π]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 1 − cos x ≥ 0, so f is increasing on [0, π] and the maximum is f(π) = π − sin π = π. The option π − 1 uses sin(π/2) = 1 instead of sin π = 0.

questions.s: For a > 0, the function f(x) = x³ − 3ax + b has local maximum value 6 and local minimum value 2. What is the value of b?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3a = 0 at x = ±√a. The local maximum is f(−√a) = 2a√a + b = 6 and the local minimum is f(√a) = −2a√a + b = 2. Adding gives 2b = 8, so b = 4 (and a√a = 1, so a = 1). The value 8 forgets to divide the sum by 2.

questions.s: Using the definition of the derivative, the derivative of f(x) = 1/x at x = 1 is lim(Δx→0) [1/(1 + Δx) − 1]/Δx. What is the value of this limit?
questions.e: 1/(1 + Δx) − 1 = −Δx/(1 + Δx), so the quotient is −1/(1 + Δx), which tends to −1. This agrees with f′(x) = −1/x² at x = 1. The answer 1 loses the minus sign in the numerator.

questions.s: If f(x) = x cos x, what is the value of f′(π)?
questions.e: Product rule: f′(x) = cos x − x sin x, so f′(π) = cos π − π sin π = −1 − 0 = −1. The value −π is f(π) = π cos π, not the derivative.

questions.s: The tangent line to y = x³ at the point where x = 2 meets the y-axis at which y-value?
questions.e: At x = 2 the point is (2, 8) and the slope is 3x² = 12, so the tangent is y − 8 = 12(x − 2), i.e. y = 12x − 16, which crosses the y-axis at −16. The value 8 is the y-coordinate of the point of tangency.

questions.s: For a > 0, the minimum value of f(x) = eˣ − ax is 0. What is the value of a?
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ − a = 0 at x = ln a, where f changes from decreasing to increasing, so the minimum is f(ln a) = a − a ln a = a(1 − ln a). Setting this to 0 gives ln a = 1, so a = e. The answer 1 would make the minimum f(0) = 1, not 0.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x³ + 3x² − 9x on the closed interval [−4, 2]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² + 6x − 9 = 3(x + 3)(x − 1) = 0 at x = −3 and x = 1. Comparing f(−4) = 20, f(−3) = 27, f(1) = −5 and f(2) = 2 gives the maximum 27. The value 20 comes from checking only the endpoints.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = x⁴ − 2x?
questions.e: By the power rule (x⁴)′ = 4x³ and (2x)′ = 2, so y′ = 4x³ − 2. The option 4x³ forgets to differentiate the term −2x, and 4x⁴ − 2 does not lower the power.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = 3 sin x − 2 cos x?
questions.e: (sin x)′ = cos x and (cos x)′ = −sin x, so y′ = 3cos x − 2(−sin x) = 3cos x + 2sin x. The option 3cos x − 2sin x forgets the minus sign in the derivative of cos x.

questions.s: If f(x) = x² + 3x, what is the value of f′(2)?
questions.e: f′(x) = 2x + 3, so f′(2) = 4 + 3 = 7. The value 10 is f(2) = 4 + 6, the function value rather than the derivative.

questions.s: An object moves with displacement s(t) = t² + t (metres, seconds). What is its average velocity between t = 1 s and t = 3 s?
questions.e: Average velocity = [s(3) − s(1)]/(3 − 1) = (12 − 2)/2 = 5 m/s. The value 10 m/s is the change in displacement without dividing by the 2 s, and 7 m/s is the instantaneous velocity s′(3).

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = 1/x (x ≠ 0)?
questions.e: Write 1/x = x⁻¹; the power rule gives −1·x⁻² = −1/x². The option ln x is an antiderivative of 1/x, not its derivative, and 1/x² loses the minus sign.

questions.s: If f(x) = eˣ, what is the value of f′(ln 3)?
questions.e: f′(x) = eˣ, so f′(ln 3) = e^(ln 3) = 3. The option e³ substitutes 3 instead of ln 3 into the exponent.

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent line to y = x³ at the point (1, 1)?
questions.e: y′ = 3x², so the slope at x = 1 is 3 and the tangent is y − 1 = 3(x − 1), i.e. y = 3x − 2. The option y = 3x − 1 has the right slope but does not pass through (1, 1).

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = x³ − 3x² decreasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 6x = 3x(x − 2) < 0 when 0 < x < 2. The interval (0, 3) comes from the zeros of f(x) = x²(x − 3), not of f′(x).

questions.s: What is the minimum value of f(x) = x² − 2x?
questions.e: f′(x) = 2x − 2 = 0 at x = 1, with f′ < 0 before and f′ > 0 after, so the minimum is f(1) = 1 − 2 = −1. The answer 1 is the x-coordinate of the minimum point.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = (x + 1)(x − 2)?
questions.e: Product rule: y′ = 1·(x − 2) + (x + 1)·1 = 2x − 1 (or expand to x² − x − 2 first). The answer 1 multiplies the derivatives of the two factors, which is not how a product is differentiated.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = (1 − x)³?
questions.e: Chain rule with u = 1 − x and u′ = −1: y′ = 3(1 − x)² × (−1) = −3(1 − x)². The option 3(1 − x)² forgets that the inner derivative is −1.

questions.s: If f′(x) = 0 for every x in an open interval, then on that interval f is
o: a linear function with nonzero slope
questions.e: A zero derivative everywhere on an interval means the tangent is horizontal at every point, so f is constant there. A linear function with nonzero slope has a constant but nonzero derivative, so it does not fit.

questions.s: A ball is thrown upward and its height is h(t) = 20t − 5t² (metres, seconds). What is its velocity at t = 3 s?
questions.e: v(t) = h′(t) = 20 − 10t, so v(3) = −10 m/s; the minus sign means the ball is falling. The value 15 is the height h(3) = 60 − 45, not the velocity.

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent line to y = 2 ln x at the point where x = 1?
questions.e: At x = 1, y = 2 ln 1 = 0 and y′ = 2/x = 2, so the tangent is y − 0 = 2(x − 1), i.e. y = 2x − 2. The option y = x − 1 is the tangent to ln x at that point, without the factor 2.

questions.s: What is the maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x + 2 on the closed interval [−2, 2]?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² − 3 = 0 at x = ±1. Comparing f(−2) = 0, f(−1) = 4, f(1) = 0 and f(2) = 4 gives the maximum 4 (reached at x = −1 and x = 2). The value 2 is just f(0), which is not a critical point.

questions.s: What is the derivative of y = x/(x² + 1)?
questions.e: Quotient rule: y′ = [1·(x² + 1) − x·2x]/(x² + 1)² = (1 − x²)/(x² + 1)². The option (x² − 1)/(x² + 1)² subtracts in the wrong order, and 1/(2x) divides the derivatives of numerator and denominator.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³ + ax has an extremum at x = 1. What is the value of a?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x² + a, and f′(1) = 3 + a = 0 gives a = −3. Check: f′(x) = 3(x² − 1) changes sign at x = 1. The answer −1 comes from setting f(1) = 1 + a = 0 instead of f′(1) = 0.

questions.s: On which interval is f(x) = xe⁻ˣ increasing?
questions.e: f′(x) = e⁻ˣ − xe⁻ˣ = (1 − x)e⁻ˣ, and e⁻ˣ > 0, so f′(x) > 0 exactly when x < 1. The interval (0, 1) is only part of it, (0, +∞) includes x > 1 where f decreases, and (1, +∞) is where f decreases.

questions.s: Positive numbers x and y satisfy x + y = 6. For which y is the product xy² largest?
questions.e: P(y) = (6 − y)y² = 6y² − y³ for 0 < y < 6. P′(y) = 12y − 3y² = 3y(4 − y) = 0 gives y = 4 (then x = 2), and P changes from increasing to decreasing there, so the maximum is 2 × 16 = 32. Choosing y = 3 assumes the numbers should be equal, which maximises xy, not xy².

questions.s: Which of the following derivative calculations is correct?
questions.e: The power rule gives (x⁻¹)′ = −x⁻². By the chain rule (sin 2x)′ = 2cos 2x and (ln 2x)′ = 2/(2x) = 1/x, and e² is a constant, so its derivative is 0, not 2e.

questions.s: The maximum value of f(x) = x³ − 3x² + a on the closed interval [−1, 1] is 2. What is the minimum value of f on this interval?
questions.e: f′(x) = 3x(x − 2), so the only critical point in [−1, 1] is x = 0. Compare f(−1) = a − 4, f(0) = a and f(1) = a − 2: the maximum is f(0) = a = 2, and the minimum is f(−1) = 2 − 4 = −2. The answer 0 uses the right endpoint f(1), which is not the smallest value.

questions.s: The line y = kx is tangent to the curve y = ln x. What is the value of k?
questions.e: Let the point of tangency be (a, ln a). The slope gives k = 1/a, and the point lies on the line: ln a = ka = 1, so a = e and k = 1/e. The answer 1 is the slope of ln x at x = 1, but the tangent there, y = x − 1, does not pass through the origin.

questions.s: The function f(x) = x³/3 − x² + ax is decreasing on the interval (1, 2). What is the range of a?
questions.e: We need f′(x) = x² − 2x + a ≤ 0 on (1, 2). Here f′ is increasing (its vertex is at x = 1), so the condition is f′(2) = a ≤ 0. The value a = 0 is allowed, since then f′(x) = x(x − 2) < 0 on (1, 2), so a < 0 is too strict; a ≤ 1 only checks f′(1) ≤ 0.

questions.s: A boat travelling at v km/h has a running cost of 800 + v³/20 yuan per hour. At which speed is the cost per kilometre smallest?
questions.e: Cost per km = (800 + v³/20)/v = 800/v + v²/20. Its derivative −800/v² + v/10 = 0 gives v³ = 8000, so v = 20 km/h, with a cost of 40 + 20 = 60 yuan per km. Minimising the hourly cost instead would wrongly favour the lowest possible speed.

questions.s: For all x > 0, the inequality x ln x ≥ m holds. What is the largest possible value of m?
questions.e: Let g(x) = x ln x; g′(x) = ln x + 1 = 0 at x = 1/e, where g changes from decreasing to increasing. So the minimum of g is g(1/e) = (1/e)(−1) = −1/e, and m can be at most −1/e. The value −1 is ln(1/e), which forgets the factor x = 1/e.

questions.s: What is the slope of the line through the points (1, 2) and (4, 8)?
questions.e: Slope = (8 − 2)/(4 − 1) = 6/3 = 2. The value 1/2 comes from dividing the change in x by the change in y, which is upside down.

questions.s: What is the inclination angle of the line x − √3y + 1 = 0?
questions.e: Rewrite as y = (1/√3)x + 1/√3, so the slope is 1/√3 = √3/3 and tan α = √3/3 gives α = 30°. Choosing 60° confuses slope √3/3 with slope √3.

questions.s: What is the inclination angle of the line √3x + y − 2 = 0?
questions.e: y = −√3x + 2, so tan α = −√3 with 0 ≤ α < π, giving α = 2π/3. π/3 ignores the negative sign of the slope; an inclination with a negative slope must be obtuse.

questions.s: A line passes through (2, −1) and has slope 3. What is its equation?
questions.e: Point-slope form: y − (−1) = 3(x − 2), so y + 1 = 3x − 6 and y = 3x − 7. y = 3x − 5 comes from writing y − 1 instead of y + 1.

questions.s: A line has x-intercept 3 and y-intercept −2. Which equation describes it?
questions.e: Intercept form: x/3 + y/(−2) = 1; multiplying by 6 gives 2x − 3y = 6, i.e. 2x − 3y − 6 = 0. The equation 3x − 2y − 6 = 0 swaps the coefficients and has intercepts 2 and −3 instead.

questions.s: The lines ax + 2y − 1 = 0 and 2x + (a − 3)y + 4 = 0 are parallel. What is the value of a?
questions.e: Parallel requires a(a − 3) = 2 × 2, so a² − 3a − 4 = 0 and a = 4 or a = −1. Checking: a = 4 gives 4x + 2y − 1 = 0 and 2x + y + 4 = 0; a = −1 gives x − 2y + 1 = 0 and x − 2y + 2 = 0. Neither pair coincides, so both values are valid.

questions.s: The lines 2x + y − 3 = 0 and x + my + 1 = 0 are perpendicular. What is m?
questions.e: For A₁x + B₁y + C₁ = 0 and A₂x + B₂y + C₂ = 0 to be perpendicular, A₁A₂ + B₁B₂ = 0: 2·1 + 1·m = 0, so m = −2. The value 1/2 is the condition for parallel lines (2m = 1).

questions.s: What is the distance from the point (1, 2) to the line 3x + 4y − 1 = 0?
questions.e: d = |3·1 + 4·2 − 1|/√(3² + 4²) = |10|/5 = 2. The answer 10 forgets to divide by √(A² + B²) = 5; 12/5 comes from using +1 instead of −1.

questions.s: What is the distance between the parallel lines 3x − 4y + 2 = 0 and 6x − 8y − 1 = 0?
questions.e: First make the coefficients equal: 6x − 8y − 1 = 0 is 3x − 4y − 1/2 = 0. Then d = |2 − (−1/2)|/√(9 + 16) = (5/2)/5 = 1/2. The value 3/5 uses C = −1 without first dividing the second equation by 2.

questions.s: What is the reflection of the point (1, 2) in the line x + y − 5 = 0?
questions.e: Reflection in x + y = 5 maps (x, y) to (5 − y, 5 − x), giving (5 − 2, 5 − 1) = (3, 4). Check: the midpoint (2, 3) lies on the line and the segment has slope 1, perpendicular to the line. (4, 3) mixes up which coordinate is subtracted.

questions.s: A line passes through the intersection of x + y − 3 = 0 and 2x − y = 0 and is perpendicular to x − 2y + 1 = 0. What is its equation?
questions.e: Adding the two equations gives 3x = 3, so the intersection is (1, 2). The given line has slope 1/2, so the required slope is −2: y − 2 = −2(x − 1), i.e. 2x + y − 4 = 0. x − 2y + 3 = 0 passes through (1, 2) but is parallel, not perpendicular, to the given line.

questions.s: A line passes through P(2, 3) and has equal non-zero intercepts on the x-axis and y-axis. What is its equation?
questions.e: Equal intercepts a give x/a + y/a = 1, i.e. x + y = a; substituting P gives a = 5, so x + y − 5 = 0. x − y + 1 = 0 has intercepts −1 and 1, which are opposite, and 3x − 2y = 0 has both intercepts zero, which the stem excludes.

questions.s: The lines x + my + 6 = 0 and (m − 2)x + 3y + 2m = 0 are parallel (and distinct). What is m?
questions.e: Parallel requires 1·3 = m(m − 2), so m² − 2m − 3 = 0 and m = 3 or m = −1. For m = 3 both equations become x + 3y + 6 = 0, so the lines coincide and m = 3 is rejected. For m = −1 the lines x − y + 6 = 0 and x − y + 2/3 = 0 are parallel, so m = −1.

questions.s: Line l is perpendicular to the line 2x − 3y + 1 = 0. What is the slope of l?
questions.e: The given line has slope 2/3. Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1, so the slope of l is −3/2. 3/2 takes the reciprocal but forgets to change the sign.

questions.s: What is the area of the triangle formed by the line 3x + 4y − 12 = 0 and the two coordinate axes?
questions.e: Setting y = 0 gives x = 4; setting x = 0 gives y = 3. The right triangle has legs 4 and 3, so its area is ½ × 4 × 3 = 6. The value 12 forgets the factor ½.

questions.s: The points A(1, 2), B(3, k) and C(5, 10) lie on one straight line. What is k?
questions.e: The slope of AC is (10 − 2)/(5 − 1) = 2. B must give the same slope from A: (k − 2)/(3 − 1) = 2, so k = 6. Since B has the midpoint x-coordinate 3, k is also the average of 2 and 10.

questions.s: As θ takes all real values, what is the range of the inclination angle α of the line x cos θ + √3y + 2 = 0?
questions.e: The slope is k = −cos θ/√3, and since −1 ≤ cos θ ≤ 1, k lies in [−√3/3, √3/3]. tan α ∈ [0, √3/3] gives α ∈ [0, π/6], and tan α ∈ [−√3/3, 0) gives α ∈ [5π/6, π). The option with π/3 and 2π/3 corresponds to slopes between −√3 and √3.

questions.s: For every real k, the line (k − 1)x − y + 2k + 1 = 0 passes through a fixed point. What is that point?
questions.e: Group the terms in k: k(x + 2) + (−x − y + 1) = 0. This holds for all k only if x + 2 = 0 and −x − y + 1 = 0, so x = −2 and y = 3. (2, 3) comes from solving x − 2 = 0 by mistake.

questions.s: A(1, 0) and B(3, 0) are fixed. Point P moves on the line x − y + 1 = 0. What is the minimum value of |PA| + |PB|?
questions.e: A and B are on the same side of the line (x − y + 1 is positive at both), so reflect A in the line. Reflection in y = x + 1 sends (x, y) to (y − 1, x + 1), so A′ = (−1, 2). The minimum is |A′B| = √(4² + 2²) = 2√5. The value 2 is |AB|, which would need P on segment AB, but AB does not meet the line.

questions.s: A(1, 2) and B(3, 4) are given. What is the equation of the perpendicular bisector of AB?
questions.e: The midpoint of AB is (2, 3) and AB has slope 1, so the bisector has slope −1: y − 3 = −(x − 2), i.e. x + y − 5 = 0. x − y + 1 = 0 also passes through (2, 3), but it is the line AB itself.

questions.s: A line has slope −2 and y-intercept 3. What is its general equation?
questions.e: Slope-intercept form gives y = −2x + 3, which rearranges to 2x + y − 3 = 0. 2x − y + 3 = 0 is y = 2x + 3, which has slope +2.

questions.s: The distance from the point (a, 2) to the line 4x − 3y + 2 = 0 is 4, and a > 0. What is a?
questions.e: |4a − 6 + 2|/5 = 4 gives |4a − 4| = 20, so 4a − 4 = ±20 and a = 6 or a = −4. Since a > 0, a = 6. −4 is the root that the condition a > 0 rejects.

questions.s: Which line passes through the origin and the intersection point of x + 2y − 4 = 0 and 2x − y − 3 = 0?
questions.e: From the second equation y = 2x − 3; substituting gives x + 4x − 6 − 4 = 0, so x = 2 and y = 1. The line through (0, 0) and (2, 1) has slope 1/2, i.e. x − 2y = 0. 2x − y = 0 has slope 2, which inverts the ratio.

questions.s: Line l passes through P(1, 2), and the points A(2, 3) and B(4, −5) are at equal distances from l. What is the equation of l?
questions.e: Either l ∥ AB or l passes through the midpoint of AB. AB has slope −8/2 = −4, giving y − 2 = −4(x − 1), i.e. 4x + y − 6 = 0. The midpoint is (3, −1); the line through (1, 2) and (3, −1) has slope −3/2, giving 3x + 2y − 7 = 0. Taking only the midpoint case misses the parallel line.

questions.s: Which statement about the line x = −2 is correct?
o: Its inclination is 0° and its slope is 0
Its inclination is 90° and it has no slope
Its inclination is 90° and its slope is 0
Its inclination is 135° and its slope is −2
questions.e: x = −2 is a vertical line, so its inclination angle is 90°, and since tan 90° is undefined, its slope does not exist. A slope of 0 belongs to horizontal lines such as y = −2, whose inclination is 0°.

questions.s: What are the centre and radius of the circle (x − 2)² + (y + 3)² = 16?
questions.e: Compare with (x − a)² + (y − b)² = r²: a = 2, b = −3 and r² = 16, so the centre is (2, −3) and r = 4. Taking (−2, 3) copies the signs inside the brackets, and 16 is r², not r.

questions.s: What are the centre and radius of the circle x² + y² + 2x − 4y − 4 = 0?
questions.e: Complete the squares: (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 4 + 1 + 4 = 9, so the centre is (−1, 2) and the radius is 3. The centre (1, −2) has the signs reversed; the centre of x² + y² + Dx + Ey + F = 0 is (−D/2, −E/2).

questions.s: The equation x² + y² + 2x − 4y + m = 0 represents a circle. What is the range of m?
questions.e: Completing squares gives (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 5 − m, which is a circle only if 5 − m > 0, i.e. m < 5. Equivalently D² + E² − 4F = 4 + 16 − 4m > 0. m < 20 forgets the factor 4 in front of F, and m = 5 gives a single point, not a circle.

questions.s: A circle has centre (1, −2) and passes through the origin. What is its equation?
questions.e: r² = (0 − 1)² + (0 + 2)² = 5, so the equation is (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = 5. Writing √5 on the right confuses r with r².

questions.s: A(−1, 2) and B(3, −4) are the ends of a diameter of a circle. What is the equation of the circle?
questions.e: The centre is the midpoint (1, −1). |AB|² = 4² + 6² = 52, so r² = (|AB|/2)² = 52/4 = 13. Using 52 treats the diameter as the radius.

questions.s: Where is the point P(1, 1) relative to the circle x² + y² − 4x + 2y − 4 = 0?
questions.e: Substitute P: 1 + 1 − 4 + 2 − 4 = −4 < 0, so P is inside. Check with standard form: (x − 2)² + (y + 1)² = 9, and the distance from P to (2, −1) is √5 < 3.

questions.s: The line 3x + 4y + m = 0 is tangent to the circle x² + y² = 4. What is m?
questions.e: Tangency means the distance from the centre (0, 0) equals the radius: |m|/5 = 2, so |m| = 10 and m = ±10. Choosing only 10 or only −10 misses one of the two parallel tangents.

questions.s: What is the length of the chord cut from the circle (x − 2)² + (y − 1)² = 4 by the line x − y + 1 = 0?
questions.e: Distance from (2, 1) to the line: |2 − 1 + 1|/√2 = √2. Half the chord is √(r² − d²) = √(4 − 2) = √2, so the chord is 2√2. √2 is only half the chord.

questions.s: What is the position of the line y = x + 3 relative to the circle x² + y² = 4?
questions.e: Write the line as x − y + 3 = 0. The distance from (0, 0) is 3/√2 = 3√2/2 ≈ 2.12, which is greater than r = 2, so the line and circle do not meet.

questions.s: What is the equation of the tangent to the circle x² + y² = 25 at the point (3, −4)?
questions.e: The tangent to x² + y² = r² at (x₀, y₀) is x₀x + y₀y = r², so 3x − 4y = 25, i.e. 3x − 4y − 25 = 0. Check: it passes through (3, −4) and is perpendicular to the radius, which has slope −4/3. 3x + 4y − 25 = 0 does not pass through (3, −4).

questions.s: What is the position of the circles x² + y² = 4 and (x − 3)² + (y − 4)² = 9 relative to each other?
questions.e: The distance between centres is √(3² + 4²) = 5, and r₁ + r₂ = 2 + 3 = 5. When the distance equals the sum of the radii, the circles touch externally.

questions.s: What is the equation of the line containing the common chord of the circles x² + y² = 10 and x² + y² − 2x − 4y = 0?
questions.e: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives 2x + 4y = 10, i.e. x + 2y − 5 = 0. Points on both circles satisfy this difference, so it is the line through both intersection points. 2x + y − 5 = 0 swaps the coefficients of x and y.

questions.s: What is the length of the common chord of the circles x² + y² = 10 and x² + y² − 2x − 4y = 0?
questions.e: Subtracting the equations gives the chord line x + 2y − 5 = 0. Its distance from the origin is 5/√5 = √5, so half the chord is √(10 − 5) = √5 and the chord is 2√5. √5 is only the half-chord.

questions.s: A tangent is drawn from P(4, 2) to the circle x² + y² − 2x − 3 = 0. What is the length of the tangent segment from P to the point of contact?
questions.e: The circle is (x − 1)² + y² = 4, centre C(1, 0), r = 2. |PC|² = 9 + 4 = 13, so the tangent length is √(13 − 4) = 3. √13 is |PC| itself, not the tangent length.

questions.s: P is a point on the circle x² + y² − 2x − 2y + 1 = 0. What is the greatest distance from P to the line x − y − 4 = 0?
questions.e: The circle is (x − 1)² + (y − 1)² = 1, centre (1, 1), r = 1. The distance from the centre to the line is |1 − 1 − 4|/√2 = 2√2, so the greatest distance is 2√2 + 1. 2√2 − 1 is the least distance.

questions.s: Which is the equation of the circle through O(0, 0), A(4, 0) and B(0, 2)?
questions.e: Angle AOB is a right angle, so AB is a diameter: centre (2, 1), r² = 5. Then (x − 2)² + (y − 1)² = 5 expands to x² + y² − 4x − 2y = 0. The version with + signs has centre (−2, −1), which does not pass through A.

questions.s: A circle has centre (2, 1) and is tangent to the line 3x + 4y + 5 = 0. What is its equation?
questions.e: The radius is the distance from the centre to the tangent: |6 + 4 + 5|/5 = 3, so r² = 9. Writing 3 on the right side uses r instead of r².

questions.s: For every real k, what is the position of the line y = k(x − 1) + 1 relative to the circle x² + y² = 4?
o: Depends on the value of k
questions.e: Every such line passes through the fixed point (1, 1), and 1² + 1² = 2 < 4, so this point is inside the circle. A line through an interior point always cuts the circle at two points, whatever k is.

questions.s: The line y = kx + 2 and the circle x² + y² = 1 have at least one common point. What is the range of k?
questions.e: Need distance ≤ radius: 2/√(1 + k²) ≤ 1, so 1 + k² ≥ 4 and k² ≥ 3. Hence k ≤ −√3 or k ≥ √3. The strict version leaves out the two tangent lines, which still have one common point.

questions.s: Which of the following equations represents a circle?
questions.e: x² + y² − 2x + 4y = 0 becomes (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = 5, a circle. With + 6 the right side becomes 5 − 6 = −1 < 0, so there are no points at all. Unequal x² and y² coefficients give an ellipse, and opposite signs give a hyperbola.

questions.s: What is the equation of the circle symmetric to (x − 1)² + (y + 2)² = 4 with respect to the line y = x?
questions.e: Reflection in y = x swaps the coordinates, so the centre (1, −2) goes to (−2, 1) and the radius stays 2: (x + 2)² + (y − 1)² = 4. (x + 1)² + (y − 2)² = 4 has centre (−1, 2), which is the reflection in the origin.

questions.s: P(1, 1) lies inside the circle x² + y² = 9. What is the length of the shortest chord through P?
questions.e: The shortest chord through P is perpendicular to OP, so its distance from the centre is |OP| = √2. Its length is 2√(9 − 2) = 2√7. The value 6 is the longest chord, the diameter.

questions.s: What is the radius of the circle x² + y² − 6y = 0?
questions.e: Complete the square: x² + (y − 3)² = 9, so the radius is 3. √6 comes from taking the square root of the coefficient 6 directly.

questions.s: P moves on the circle x² + y² = 4 and Q is the fixed point (4, 0). What is the equation of the locus of the midpoint M of PQ?
questions.e: Let M = (x, y). Then P = (2x − 4, 2y), and P lies on the circle: (2x − 4)² + (2y)² = 4, which simplifies to (x − 2)² + y² = 1. The radius 4 forgets that halving the segment also halves the radius.

questions.s: The circles x² + y² = 1 and x² + y² − 6x − 8y + m = 0 are externally tangent. What is m?
questions.e: The second circle has centre (3, 4) and radius √(25 − m). The centres are 5 apart, so external tangency needs 1 + √(25 − m) = 5, giving 25 − m = 16 and m = 9. m = −11 gives radius 6, which is internal tangency.

questions.s: What are the coordinates of the foci of the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1?
questions.e: a² = 25 is under x², so the foci are on the x-axis, and c² = a² − b² = 25 − 9 = 16, so c = 4 and the foci are (±4, 0). (±√34, 0) adds a² and b², which is the hyperbola rule.

questions.s: What is the eccentricity of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/12 = 1?
questions.e: a = 4 and c² = 16 − 12 = 4, so c = 2 and e = c/a = 2/4 = 1/2. √3/2 is b/a = √12/4, not c/a; an ellipse always has 0 < e < 1, which also rules out 2.

questions.s: What are the lengths of the major and minor axes of the ellipse 4x² + y² = 16?
questions.e: Dividing by 16 gives x²/4 + y²/16 = 1, so a = 4 (on the y-axis) and b = 2. The major axis is 2a = 8 and the minor axis is 2b = 4. The pair 4 and 2 gives the semi-axes, not the axes.

questions.s: An ellipse has foci (±3, 0) and major axis of length 10. What is its standard equation?
questions.e: 2a = 10 gives a = 5, and c = 3, so b² = a² − c² = 25 − 9 = 16. The foci are on the x-axis, so a² goes under x²: x²/25 + y²/16 = 1. x²/16 + y²/25 = 1 would put the foci on the y-axis.

questions.s: P is a point on the ellipse x²/16 + y²/7 = 1 with foci F₁ and F₂. If |PF₁| = 3, what is |PF₂|?
questions.e: For any point on an ellipse, |PF₁| + |PF₂| = 2a. Here a = 4, so |PF₂| = 8 − 3 = 5. The value 8 is 2a itself, the whole sum.

questions.s: F₁ and F₂ are the foci of the ellipse x²/9 + y²/5 = 1. A chord AB passes through F₁. What is the perimeter of triangle ABF₂?
questions.e: |AF₁| + |AF₂| = 2a and |BF₁| + |BF₂| = 2a, and |AF₁| + |BF₁| = |AB|. So the perimeter is |AB| + |AF₂| + |BF₂| = 4a = 12. The value 6 is 2a, counting only one of the two points.

questions.s: The ellipse x²/m + y²/4 = 1 has focal distance |F₁F₂| = 2. What is m?
questions.e: 2c = 2 gives c = 1. If m > 4, the foci are on the x-axis and m − 4 = 1, so m = 5; if 0 < m < 4, the foci are on the y-axis and 4 − m = 1, so m = 3. Both cases are possible, so m = 3 or 5.

questions.s: The equation x²/(k − 2) + y²/(6 − k) = 1 represents an ellipse with foci on the x-axis. What is the range of k?
questions.e: Foci on the x-axis need k − 2 > 6 − k > 0. The first inequality gives k > 4 and the second gives k < 6, so 4 < k < 6. 2 < k < 6 only makes both denominators positive and includes k = 4, which gives a circle.

questions.s: An ellipse with centre at the origin and major axis on the x-axis passes through (2, 0) and has eccentricity √3/2. What is its equation?
questions.e: (2, 0) is a vertex on the major axis, so a = 2. Then c = ea = √3 and b² = 4 − 3 = 1, giving x²/4 + y² = 1. x²/4 + y²/3 = 1 uses b² = 3, which is c², not b².

questions.s: P moves on the ellipse x²/9 + y²/4 = 1 with foci F₁ and F₂. What is the greatest area of triangle PF₁F₂?
questions.e: c = √(9 − 4) = √5, so the base F₁F₂ = 2√5. The height is greatest when P is at an end of the minor axis, height b = 2. Area = ½ × 2√5 × 2 = 2√5. Using height 3 (= a) gives 3√5, but no point of the ellipse is 3 units from the x-axis.

questions.s: P is a point on the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 with foci F₁ and F₂, and ∠F₁PF₂ = 90°. What is the area of triangle F₁PF₂?
questions.e: Let |PF₁| = m and |PF₂| = n. Then m + n = 2a = 10 and m² + n² = (2c)² = 64. So 2mn = 100 − 64 = 36, mn = 18, and the area is ½mn = 9 (equal to b² when the angle is 90°). 16 is c², not b².

questions.s: The two foci of an ellipse and one end of its minor axis are the vertices of an equilateral triangle. What is the eccentricity?
questions.e: The distance from an end of the minor axis to each focus is √(b² + c²) = a, and the foci are 2c apart. Equilateral means a = 2c, so e = c/a = 1/2. √3/2 would come from taking b = c√3 as if the triangle's side were 2b.

questions.s: A chord of the ellipse x²/16 + y²/4 = 1 has midpoint (2, 1). What is the equation of the line containing the chord?
questions.e: For chord ends (x₁, y₁), (x₂, y₂), subtracting the two ellipse equations gives (x₁² − x₂²)/16 + (y₁² − y₂²)/4 = 0, so the slope is −(4 × 4)/(16 × 2) = −1/2 (using x₁ + x₂ = 4, y₁ + y₂ = 2). The line is y − 1 = −½(x − 2), i.e. x + 2y − 4 = 0. x − 2y = 0 is the line through the origin and the midpoint, not the chord.

questions.s: F₁ and F₂ are fixed points with |F₁F₂| = 8. What is the set of points P with |PF₁| + |PF₂| = 8?
questions.e: By the triangle inequality |PF₁| + |PF₂| ≥ |F₁F₂| = 8, with equality exactly when P lies on segment F₁F₂. An ellipse needs the constant sum to be greater than |F₁F₂|.

questions.s: The line y = x + 1 meets the ellipse x²/2 + y² = 1 at A and B. What is |AB|?
questions.e: Substituting gives x²/2 + (x + 1)² = 1, i.e. (3/2)x² + 2x = 0, so x = 0 or x = −4/3. Since the slope is 1, |AB| = √(1 + 1²) × |x₁ − x₂| = √2 × 4/3 = 4√2/3. 4/3 forgets the factor √(1 + k²).

questions.s: An ellipse has centre at the origin, foci on the y-axis, semi-major axis 3 and eccentricity 2/3. What is its equation?
questions.e: a = 3 and c = ea = 2, so b² = 9 − 4 = 5. With foci on the y-axis, a² goes under y²: x²/5 + y²/9 = 1. x²/4 + y²/9 = 1 uses c² instead of b².

questions.s: The ellipse x²/a² + y²/b² = 1 (a > b > 0) passes through (2, 0) and (1, 3/2). What is its equation?
questions.e: (2, 0) gives a² = 4. Then 1/4 + (9/4)/b² = 1 gives (9/4)/b² = 3/4, so b² = 3. Check x²/4 + y² = 1: at x = 1 it gives y = ±√3/2, not 3/2.

questions.s: An ellipse with foci F₁ and F₂ has a point P with ∠F₁PF₂ = 90°. What is the range of its eccentricity e?
questions.e: The angle F₁PF₂ is largest at an end of the minor axis, so a right angle is possible only if, there, c ≥ b. Then c² ≥ a² − c², so e² ≥ 1/2 and e ≥ √2/2; with e < 1 this gives [√2/2, 1). (0, √2/2] reverses the inequality.

questions.s: What are the end points of the major axis of the ellipse 9x² + 4y² = 36?
questions.e: Dividing by 36 gives x²/4 + y²/9 = 1. The larger denominator 9 is under y², so the major axis is on the y-axis with a = 3, and its end points are (0, ±3). (±2, 0) are the ends of the minor axis.

questions.s: P(x, y) moves on the ellipse x²/3 + y² = 1. What is the greatest value of x + y?
questions.e: Write x = √3 cos θ and y = sin θ. Then x + y = √3 cos θ + sin θ = 2 sin(θ + π/3), whose greatest value is 2. √3 + 1 adds the separate maxima of x and y, which are not reached at the same point.

questions.s: A point P on the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 has x-coordinate 5/2. What is the distance from P to the left focus F₁(−4, 0)?
questions.e: y² = 9(1 − 1/4) = 27/4. Then |PF₁|² = (5/2 + 4)² + 27/4 = 169/4 + 27/4 = 49, so |PF₁| = 7 (the focal radius formula a + ex₀ = 5 + (4/5)(5/2) gives the same). 3 is the distance to the right focus.

questions.s: F is the left focus of the ellipse x²/4 + y²/3 = 1 and P moves on the ellipse. What is the range of |PF|?
questions.e: a = 2 and c = √(4 − 3) = 1. The distance from a focus is least at the near vertex (a − c = 1) and greatest at the far vertex (a + c = 3), so |PF| ∈ [1, 3]. [√3, 2] is the range of the distance from the centre, from b to a.

questions.s: How does the shape of an ellipse change as its eccentricity e gets closer to 1?
o: It becomes rounder, closer to a circle
It becomes flatter and more elongated
It keeps the same shape but grows
It turns into a pair of lines
questions.e: b/a = √(1 − e²), so as e approaches 1, b/a approaches 0 and the ellipse becomes flatter. As e approaches 0, b/a approaches 1 and the ellipse looks more like a circle.

questions.s: A line through the right focus of the ellipse x²/2 + y² = 1 is perpendicular to the x-axis. What is the length of the chord it cuts from the ellipse?
questions.e: c = √(2 − 1) = 1, so the line is x = 1. Then y² = 1 − 1/2 = 1/2, y = ±√2/2, and the chord has length √2 (equal to 2b²/a = 2/√2). √2/2 is only half of it.

questions.s: F₁ and F₂ are the left and right foci of x²/4 + y²/3 = 1. P is on the ellipse with |PF₁| − |PF₂| = 1. What is cos∠F₁PF₂?
questions.e: |PF₁| + |PF₂| = 4 and |PF₁| − |PF₂| = 1 give 5/2 and 3/2, and |F₁F₂| = 2c = 2. Cosine rule: cos∠F₁PF₂ = (25/4 + 9/4 − 4)/(2 × 5/2 × 3/2) = (9/2)/(15/2) = 3/5. A negative value would need an obtuse angle, but 25/4 + 9/4 > 4.

questions.s: What are the asymptotes of the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1?
questions.e: For x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 the asymptotes are y = ±(b/a)x. Here a = 3 and b = 4, so y = ±(4/3)x. y = ±(3/4)x uses a/b, which is the rule for a hyperbola with foci on the y-axis.

questions.s: What are the coordinates of the foci of the hyperbola x²/4 − y²/5 = 1?
questions.e: For a hyperbola c² = a² + b² = 4 + 5 = 9, so c = 3. The x² term is positive, so the foci are on the x-axis: (±3, 0). (±1, 0) uses the ellipse rule c² = a² − b² with the values swapped.

questions.s: What is the eccentricity of the hyperbola x² − y²/3 = 1?
questions.e: a = 1, b = √3, so c = √(1 + 3) = 2 and e = c/a = 2. 2√3/3 divides c by b instead of by a.

questions.s: What is the length of the real (transverse) axis of the hyperbola y²/16 − x²/9 = 1?
questions.e: The positive term is y²/16, so a² = 16, a = 4 and the real axis has length 2a = 8. 6 is the imaginary axis 2b, and 10 is the focal distance 2c.

questions.s: A hyperbola has foci (±√5, 0) and asymptotes y = ±½x. What is its equation?
questions.e: b/a = 1/2, so a = 2b, and a² + b² = c² = 5 gives 5b² = 5, so b = 1 and a = 2. The equation is x²/4 − y² = 1. x² − y²/4 = 1 has asymptotes y = ±2x.

questions.s: A hyperbola has its foci on the x-axis and asymptotes y = ±√3x. What is its eccentricity?
questions.e: b/a = √3, so e = c/a = √(1 + b²/a²) = √(1 + 3) = 2. 2√3/3 is the eccentricity when the foci are on the y-axis (then a/b = √3).

questions.s: P is a point on the hyperbola x²/9 − y²/16 = 1 with foci F₁ and F₂. If |PF₁| = 7, what is |PF₂|?
questions.e: ||PF₁| − |PF₂|| = 2a = 6, so |PF₂| = 1 or 13. But c = 5, and every point of the hyperbola is at least c − a = 2 from a focus, so 1 is impossible and |PF₂| = 13. Keeping both values forgets this check.

questions.s: A rectangular (equilateral) hyperbola with centre at the origin and axes along the coordinate axes passes through (3, −1). What is its equation?
questions.e: Such a hyperbola is x² − y² = λ (λ ≠ 0). Substituting (3, −1) gives λ = 9 − 1 = 8, so x² − y² = 8. x² − y² = 10 adds the squares instead of subtracting.

questions.s: A hyperbola has the same asymptotes as x²/4 − y²/9 = 1 and passes through (4, 3). What is its equation?
questions.e: Hyperbolas with these asymptotes are x²/4 − y²/9 = λ. At (4, 3): 16/4 − 9/9 = 3, so λ = 3 and the equation is x²/12 − y²/27 = 1. The y²-first version would need λ < 0.

questions.s: What is the distance from a focus of the hyperbola x²/4 − y²/12 = 1 to one of its asymptotes?
questions.e: c = √(4 + 12) = 4, focus (4, 0), asymptote √3x − y = 0. Distance = |4√3|/√(3 + 1) = 2√3, which equals b, as it does for every hyperbola. 2 is a, not b.

questions.s: A hyperbola x²/a² − y²/b² = 1 has eccentricity 2, and the distance from a focus to an asymptote is √3. What is its equation?
questions.e: The focus-to-asymptote distance equals b, so b = √3. e = 2 gives c = 2a, and c² = a² + b² gives 4a² = a² + 3, so a = 1. The equation is x² − y²/3 = 1. x²/4 − y²/12 = 1 also has e = 2, but its focus-to-asymptote distance is 2√3.

questions.s: The equation x²/(m − 1) + y²/(m − 4) = 1 represents a hyperbola. What is the range of m?
questions.e: A hyperbola needs the two denominators to have opposite signs: (m − 1)(m − 4) < 0, so 1 < m < 4. If m < 1 both denominators are negative and there are no points; if m > 4 both are positive and the curve is an ellipse.

questions.s: A hyperbola has the same foci as the ellipse x²/25 + y²/9 = 1 and its eccentricity is 2. What is its equation?
